Karthik/Soojin/Marissa: I'm escalating this as a priority-1 for today. Quick asks:

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-09-16T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: p95 spike (08:10 PT) — proposed triage + temporary mitigations

Quick triage notes (observed 08:10–08:55 PT):
- Root cause signal: KV cache miss rate jumped ~6x on Checkoutly routes; concurrent token fanout increased (many small requests with high max_tokens).
- Downstream effect: request queuing on the serving runtime produced p95 jumps; no immediate OOMs.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (can be applied per-customer):
1) Set per-customer concurrency cap to 8 (down from 24) for Checkoutly. Estimated p95 reduction: 45–60% within 2–4 minutes. Command: redwoodctl config set --customer checkoutly --concurrency_limit 8 --scope route
2) Enable a 30s emergency queue with request dropping at 120s to prevent backlog amplification. Command: redwoodctl config set --customer checkoutly --queue_max_age 30s --queue_drop_after 120s
3) Kick KV warmup for hot prefixes used by Checkoutly: redwoodctl cache warmup --customer checkoutly --prefixes cart,session

Rollback plan: revert concurrency_limit to 24 and queue settings; we will monitor p99/p95 for 10m after change.

I can apply 1+2 immediately if you give me the go-ahead. Attaching snapshot-metrics-0916.png (token distribution + cache miss graph).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-09-16T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: p95 spike (08:10 PT) — product tradeoffs and short-term policy

Thanks — I agree with Karthik's mitigations as an immediate containment. Two product notes / asks before we flip anything that changes model behavior:
1) Quantization fallback: we can enable a route-scoped lower-precision inference path (dynamic fallback to int8 on non-critical routes) but there's a measurable drop in long-form coherence on high max_tokens. If Checkoutly runs high max_tokens for summaries, we should not silently degrade without telling them.
2) Temporary request-level limits: lowering max_tokens to 512 for a 2-hour window is less risky than quantization fallback for generative quality. That would prevent the largest fanout requests.

Proposed short-term product-approved options (pick one):
A) Per-route concurrency cap (Karthik's suggestion) + temporary max_tokens=512 for Checkoutly for 2 hours. Low risk to quality, high chance to stabilize.
B) Per-route concurrency cap + route-scoped dynamic int8 fallback for 2 hours. Faster stabilization but risk of regression on longer outputs — CS must ask Checkoutly to validate outputs post-change.

If CS confirms Checkoutly is willing to accept slight quality changes, we can do B; otherwise approve A. Also recommend we add a roadmap ticket to build route-level adaptive batching + prefix-preserving cache warmups (ETA Q1 2030).

Soojin Lee
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Date: 2029-09-16T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Containment update + customer note (draft) — Checkoutly token surge

Matt / Lina —

Thanks for the quick signal earlier. We implemented a targeted containment plan for the Checkoutly routes and want to share what we did and the expected impact:

What we implemented (09/16 09:05 PT):
- Reduced per-customer concurrency for Checkoutly to 8 (from 24).
- Enabled a short emergency queue (30s) and set a guard to drop requests after 120s to prevent backlog amplification.
- Triggered KV warmup for your hot prefixes (cart, session).

Expected impact:
- We expect p95 to drop by ~50% within minutes; p99 to show progressive improvement as warmups complete.
- We do not anticipate increased error rates from these changes; they primarily throttle concurrency to protect overall throughput.

Temporary product change (for stability):
- We recommend option A (concurrency cap + temporary max_tokens cap of 512 for 2 hours) to avoid any potential quality regression. Please let us know if you'd prefer we instead try a quantization fallback (which may affect longer-generation quality).

Next steps:
- Please confirm whether you accept the temporary max_tokens cap. If yes we'll put the policy in place immediately.
- We'll monitor and share a short postmortem and next-step roadmap items (adaptive batching + cache warmup improvements).

Draft customer-facing note (please review):
---
Subject: Temporary rate-limiting to stabilize checkouts (Sept 16)
Hi Checkoutly team —
We saw increased latencies that affected some checkout requests this morning. We've applied a targeted concurrency limit and short-term safeguards to stabilize your traffic. We expect normal performance to return within the next 30–60 minutes as caches warm. We'll follow up with a concise root-cause summary and actions.
If you notice regressions in outputs or have a preferred option (lower token cap vs quantization fallback), please reply here and we'll adjust.
---

Attached: cust_comm_draft_0916.docx (word draft).

Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
